overall_summary: Space-themed content focusing on extreme, paradoxical physical phenomena (e.g., burning ice, space oceans, smelling like steak) is the primary growth driver for FACTVERSE. In contrast, abstract psychology topics and generic brain facts struggle to gain traction, consistently underperforming.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' achieved 1,053 views, 'The Largest Ocean in Space' reached 460 views, and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' hit 368 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space anomalies that present physical contradictions (e.g., cold stars, liquid metal rains) using highly visual, paradoxical hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' generated 302 views, significantly outperforming standard animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (183 views).
winning_patterns.action: Create comparison-based shorts that challenge the viewer's understanding of historical timelines or evolutionary biology.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) failed to capture audience interest.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract psychological concepts; if covering human biology, pivot to bizarre medical anomalies or historical mysteries instead.

experiment: Test a 'Time-Scale Comparison' short (e.g., comparing the construction of the Pyramids to the lifespan of Woolly Mammoths) to see if historical timeline paradoxes can replicate the high engagement of space anomalies.
